page: Amazon Web Services r5b.12xlarge is a memory-optimized fifth-generation server instance built on the Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8259CL processor running at 3.1 GHz. The configuration delivers 48 virtual CPUs across 24 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. Memory capacity is 384.0 GB of DDR4 RAM operating at 3 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of memory per core. The instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 12 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates average multi-core performance and weak single-core performance. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance and single-threaded gzip compression both rank in the bottom 25 percent, highlighting a trade-off in single-threaded execution speed. Conversely, multi-core metrics, including stress-ng multi-core CPU performance, Geekbench multi-core, and PassMark CPU scores, fall consistently within the middle 50 percent. Memory bandwidth tests for both small cached blocks and large uncached blocks also demonstrate average performance.

Given the high memory-to-vCPU ratio and average multi-threaded capabilities, this instance is suited for memory-intensive workloads such as database operations, caching layers, and medium-scale data processing. PassMark database operations and Redis SET operations both perform in the average tier. The lack of local storage requires reliance on network-attached storage, which should be factored into the overall architectural cost efficiency. The hardware profile offers a balanced resource density for enterprise applications that require substantial memory footprints without demanding top-tier single-core compute performance.
